old: Postpositions *emlékére* ('in memory of') and *tiszteletére* ('in honor of') take a noun in the nominative/possessive: *A honfoglalás ezeréves évfordulójának emlékére épült a Hősök tere.* ('Heroes' Square was built in memory of the thousand-year anniversary of the Conquest.').
new: *Emlékére* ('in memory of') and *tiszteletére* ('in honour of') are possessive nouns (*emléke*, *tisztelete*) with the ending *-re* (you know *-ra/-re* from A2 Unit 6 and possessive endings from A2 Unit 3). The person or event comes before them, with or without *-nak/-nek*: *a honfoglalás emlékére*, *a honfoglalás ezeréves évfordulójának emlékére építették a Hősök terét.* ('They built Heroes' Square in memory of the thousandth anniversary of the Conquest.')
why: the screen calls them postpositions that take a noun in the nominative/possessive, which misstates the pattern

old: In honor of the Hungarian nation, a grandiose exhibition was organized in the City Park.
new: In honour of the Hungarian nation, a large exhibition was organized in the City Park.

old: Prefixes *ki-*, *át-*, and *létre-* denote comprehensive urban transformations: *kiépül a sugárút* (the avenue is fully built out), *világvárossá alakul át a főváros* (the capital transforms into a world metropolis), *létrejön az egységes Budapest* (unified Budapest comes into existence).
new: You know verbal prefixes from A1 Unit 28 and A2 Unit 22. Three verbs with prefixes describe a changing city: *kiépül* ('is built out'), *átalakul* ('is transformed') and *létrejön* ('comes into being'): *kiépült a sugárút* ('the avenue was built out'), *a főváros nagyvárossá alakult át* ('the capital was transformed into a large city'), *létrejött az egységes Budapest* ('unified Budapest came into being'). In a neutral sentence the prefix stands right before the verb.
why: screen presents prefixes as new (A1 Unit 28, A2 Unit 22); figurative létre- / focus inversion examples are B2
